# Request Network Lets Payment Platforms Run All Their Merchants From One Dashboard


Operations teams can now onboard, monetize, brand and set up wallet screening rules for every merchant themselves, from one dashboard.


Request Network


October 29, 2026


**Zug, Switzerland, 29/10/26.** Today Request Network, a major Web3 payment protocol since 2017, announced the launch of its orchestrator dashboard. It is built for the payment platforms, gateways and marketplaces that connect their merchants to stablecoin collections and payouts through Request Network, and earn a fee on every payment they connect.


From today, the orchestrator dashboard puts every merchant’s setup in one place, and the people who run merchant operations can change it themselves.


## **Bring a new merchant live in minutes, under your own brand.**


The operations team now onboards new merchants directly from the dashboard, with no tech team involved. They create an onboarding link and send it to the merchant. The link opens an onboarding flow that carries the payment platform’s own branding. The merchant completes the setup in four steps: they connect their wallet, choose their settlement destination (the chain and stablecoin they want to be paid in), and select their wallet screening providers when the platform leaves that choice to them. Each merchant’s setup then appears in the dashboard, so the team can bring on many merchants and still see how each one is configured.


Platforms that need to automate onboarding or run it at scale can do the same programmatically through the API.


*The merchant onboards in four steps.*


## **White-label every payment page with your brand or your merchant’s.**


Payment platforms now choose whose brand appears on every payment page either their own or the merchant’s. The name, colors and logo are set once in the dashboard and applied to every payment page, with no development work. Payers see a brand they already know, and the payment experience stays the paltform’s or the merchant’s.


*The platform’’s name, colors and logo, set once for every payment page.*


## **Monetize every payment, and override fees for any merchant.**


Different fee setups across merchants, even complex ones, are now managed in a few clicks from the dashboard instead of through the API. Orchestrators set one default fee for all merchants, then override it for any merchant whose agreement is different. Fees can be set separately on collections and payouts, and the orchestrator chooses whether the payer or the merchant pays them. Each fee is split on-chain in the same transaction and sent to the orchestrator’s wallet, so the orchestrator collects its margin on every payment without ever holding merchant funds.


*The default fees, applied to every merchant.*


*A merchant-specific fee overriding the default.*


## **Screen every wallet, with standard rules or your own.**


Payment platforms can now set up and manage wallet screening from the dashboard. When creating an onboarding link, they choose whether to enforce screening for that merchant. If they do, they select a primary and a backup provider, Hypernative or Merkle Science, and either apply the standard rules or use their own provider API keys and custom KYT rules. Otherwise, the merchant chooses its own provider during onboarding. When screening is on and a wallet fails the check, the payment does not initiate and funds never move.


*A primary and a backup screening provider, running on the platform’s own provider account.*


## **Delegate the day-to-day, keep control of what matters.**


Payment platforms can now give their whole team access to the dashboard without sharing control of sensitive settings. Team members handle day-to-day merchant management, such as onboarding new merchants and adjusting their setup. Only the super admin, the person who set up the platform’s dashboard, can change the wallets that receive fees, set screening providers and rules, and grant or revoke access. By design, no one else on the team can ever change where the platform’s fees are paid.


*What each team member can change, and every access in one place.*


## **Manage your whole merchant base from one list.**


Orchestrators now see every merchant connected to them in one list, with its client ID and onboarding status. For each merchant, the team can see who onboarded it, export the full list as a CSV, and deactivate any merchant when needed, without involving the tech team.


## **The orchestrator dashboard is live today**


Payment platforms create their orchestrator ID with a single API call from their wallet, as described at[docs.request.network/orchestrators](https://docs.request.network/orchestrators/overview) , and the dashboard appears the next time they connect their wallet.


If you need guidance, please[contact us](https://request.network/contact/) .


## **About Request Network**


Since 2017,[Request Network](https://request.network/) has developed, educated about, and promoted the use of open-source, decentralized and permissionless protocols that provide infrastructure for on-chain payments and related financial flows.


Request Network allows anyone to send and receive stablecoins at scale, across chains, without custodial intermediaries. The protocol is developed by a community-funded foundation whose mission is to make stablecoin payments accessible while protecting its participants.


To date, more than $2 billion has moved thanks to Request Network technology.
